lines.en: 「“······Captain, what did you just say?”」
What brought me to my senses was Shin Yoosung’s incredulous voice.
「“Say that again. What the hell did you just say? What? A companion?”
“That man is your companion, Captain?”」
Yoo Joonghyuk did not respond to her disbelieving voice.
······Even I was surprised. How much more shocked must Shin Yoosung have been?
To think that Yoo Joonghyuk, with all his pride, would call me his ‘companion.’
······This was suddenly getting scary.
No matter how I thought about it, there was no way that bastard would call me his ‘companion’······.
Wouldn’t that bastard kill me all over again the moment he saw me resurrect later?
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ is moved by your comradeship.]
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ grows misty-eyed at your comradeship.]
[You have received a donation of 500 coins.]
······Right. Now it made sense.
Yoo Joonghyuk, that bastard was definitely angling for donations.
It was a little odd that Uriel, who loved comradeship, was nowhere to be seen, but either way, this had to be a masterstroke aimed at getting donations.
Watching him shout in that solemn voice while bleeding profusely, my suspicion gradually turned to certainty.

Besides, considering that Yoo Joonghyuk was still in his third round, the word ‘companion’ wasn’t entirely out of the question. In the early rounds of the original novel, he had spouted that word when Lee Hyunsung or Lee Seolhwa died, too.
It stung to think of the enormous number of coins he must be receiving right now.
Thinking about it that way chased away every bit of the emotion that had been welling up.
Damn it. I should have been the one to say that line.
「“Captain······how can you say something like that?”」
Of course, Shin Yoosung, who didn’t know what Yoo Joonghyuk was really thinking, looked as though the world had ended.
She could hardly have looked any other way.
Especially the Shin Yoosung of the forty-first round······.
Because, right up until that round ended, she had never once heard the word ‘companion’ from Yoo Joonghyuk.
Krrrraaaack!
Shin Yoosung’s fist collided with Yoo Joonghyuk’s blade.

Although it was a fight between flesh and a weapon, it was Yoo Joonghyuk’s sword that was taking damage. The SS-grade Splitting the Sky Sword (振天覇刀). It had no special options, but its durability and strength were exceptional. And that sword was crying out in pain beneath Shin Yoosung’s bare fists.
Crrrunch.
In the end, unable to withstand the impact, the Splitting the Sky Sword’s blade bent. The invincible sword, wreathed in Splitting the Sky Energy, was bowing its body helplessly.
「“How, how dare you say that in front of me!”」
She hadn’t even used some incredible skill. Just a single blow that hurled out ether compressed to its utmost limit.
Booooom!
That one blow sent Yoo Joonghyuk flying backward, spewing blood.
In attack, in speed, in variation.
Shin Yoosung surpassed Yoo Joonghyuk in every respect.
Even the [Red Phoenix Shunpo] and [Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship] that Yoo Joonghyuk took such pride in were losing their luster before Shin Yoosung at this moment.
With horrific sounds of rupturing flesh (破肉音), Yoo Joonghyuk’s face was snapped from side to side without respite.
It was a matter of time, not talent.

Even if she had descended in a weakened state, the Shin Yoosung of the forty-first round had grown almost to the limit of what Shin Yoosung could achieve as a [Beast Lord]. By contrast, however strong this round’s Yoo Joonghyuk might be, he was still only the Yoo Joonghyuk of the early stages.
「“Why do you call that man your companion? Because he sacrificed himself for you? Just because of that?”」
Streams of blood spurting out ceaselessly in choking bursts.
Even so, Yoo Joonghyuk did not yield.
Without yielding, he kept swinging his sword.
That idiot. Why the hell was he fighting?
Watching Yoo Joonghyuk bleed from all over his body, I began to feel increasingly frustrated.
If he knew he was at a disadvantage, shouldn’t he have run away long ago?
He was usually so good at that. So why?
Shin Yoosung threw another punch and spoke.
「“Then what were the others and I to you? Jihye-unnie, Hyunsung-oppa. And Seolhwa-unnie? What the hell did the people who fought only for you mean to you?”
“I······don’t know what you’re talking about.”
“What?”
“There is only one thing I know.”
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke as he wiped his bloodstained lips.
“You killed my companion in this round. So you, too, will die.”」
Damn it. This time, emotion welled up despite myself.
[Some functions of ‘Fourth Wall’ are restricted due to excessive immersion.]
Even if it was all an act, a performance like that made me think I wouldn’t mind being fooled.
Right. This was what I read ‘Ways of Survival’ for.
Come to think of it, I seemed to remember getting misty-eyed when Yoo Joonghyuk said something similar to the dead Lee Hyunsung.
Suddenly, my feelings were all over the place.
To think that I, a mere reader, had become the ‘companion’ of none other than the protagonist, Yoo Joonghyuk.
Shin Yoosung looked at Yoo Joonghyuk as though she had lost everything.
「“You can’t do that······.”」
An ominous aura was consuming the space around her. Emptiness turning to a sense of betrayal, and that sense of betrayal turning again to anger.
「“I can’t let you change like that now.”」
Terrifying ether gathering in Shin Yoosung’s fist.
I had considered watching a little longer because seeing him get so thoroughly beaten was rather enjoyable, but a sense of danger swept over me. I couldn’t let this go on.
[Proficiency in ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint’ increases dramatically due to excessive immersion.]
Because at this rate, Yoo Joonghyuk really might die.
Then everything would truly be ruined.
I quickly switched the mode of ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint.’
From third-person observer viewpoint to first-person protagonist viewpoint.
[Changing the viewpoint to first person.]
[Failed to change to ‘First-Person Protagonist’s Viewpoint.’]
What? Why?
[The conditions for changing viewpoints have not been met.]
It felt like I had been struck in the back of the head.
There were two conditions for using ‘First-Person Protagonist’s Viewpoint.’
One: I had to be dead and in an out-of-body state.
Two: the person I was entering and I had to be thinking of each other at the same time.
I had met the first condition, so the problem was the second. But there was no way that one hadn’t been met.
That bastard wasn’t thinking about me right now?
Then what the hell was all that raging about taking revenge?
Watching Yoo Joonghyuk frantically unleash one sword strike after another, I went blank for a moment.
「“I’ll kill you. I will kill you, no matter what.”」
······Was that bastard perhaps not thinking at all?
Shin Yoosung, who had been watching Yoo Joonghyuk quietly, spoke.
「“······This won’t do. I was going to end this quickly, but I’ve changed my mind.”」
A demonic smile settled on Shin Yoosung’s lips.
「“I’ll end your world in the most horrific way possible, Captain.”」
Shin Yoosung turned her gaze elsewhere, away from Yoo Joonghyuk. The moment I followed it, my heart sank.
Damn it. Now I really couldn’t just watch.
It didn’t have to be Yoo Joonghyuk. If I didn’t enter someone else, anyone else······.
At that moment, a sharp sensation flashed through my mind.
Someone I hadn’t expected was thinking of me.
······I could enter this character?
That couldn’t be possible, could it?
Oh. Was that it?
Because Yoo Joonghyuk had just said those words······?
Right. Perhaps entering this person would be better.
I didn’t know. I’d just try whatever I could.
I began projecting all my mental strength into that character.
And a little later.
My vision swayed, and dizzying nausea washed over me.
[Changing the viewpoint to first person.]
As my surroundings shifted, my consciousness was sucked somewhere else.
‘A companion?’
The moment she first heard those words, Shin Yoosung could not believe her ears.
A companion. How could he possibly say such a thing?
Yoo Joonghyuk, of all people.
Shin Yoosung could not understand the turmoil stirring deep within her chest at that moment. It awakened an emotion she had forgotten over the course of a thousand years.
That Yoo Joonghyuk, saying ‘companion.’
She didn’t know what on earth had happened to Yoo Joonghyuk. But if those words were true, if it was the Yoo Joonghyuk of this round, perhaps, even to me······.
Booooom!
Before she knew it, Shin Yoosung had struck the ground.
‘Despicable.’
That was what Shin Yoosung thought. And because she thought that.
“This is your last chance.”
She could not possibly forgive herself for entertaining such a despicable thought.
“Take it back, even now, and I’ll send you off without pain. Say it yourself. Say you have no companions, that you’re a man who cares only about himself. Say it right now.”
Even reduced to a bloody pulp, Yoo Joonghyuk did not answer.
One arm had been crushed by Shin Yoosung’s blows, and the muscles in his legs were shredded. Even so, the proud light in Yoo Joonghyuk’s eyes was still alive.
Shin Yoosung watched him for a moment, then ground her teeth.
“Hold Yoo Joonghyuk.”

At Shin Yoosung’s command, the grade-6 [Sulfur Mummy] monsters that had crossed through [Monster Gate] began to move. As the mummies’ snow-white bandages bound Yoo Joonghyuk’s entire body, his limbs were pulled taut, as though they might tear off at any moment. Shin Yoosung spoke to him.
“I’ll kill them one by one, Captain. Right before your eyes, in the most painful way possible.”
Leaving Yoo Joonghyuk behind, Shin Yoosung walked toward the edge of the island.
“Kill her! That bitch is the disaster!”
Incarnations who had spotted Shin Yoosung were crawling up from the water’s edge one after another. She lightly swept her hand toward them, from left to right.
Slaaaash!
At that light movement of her hand, the charging incarnations were torn apart like waterlogged newspaper. A slaughter that left no time even to scream.
“Overflow.”
At that single word, monsters poured out of [Monster Gate]. The two most powerful among them stood behind her, as though serving as her guards.
The grade-5 sea monster species, King Masswood.
The grade-5 monster species, Heavy Metal Kong.
Monsters powerful enough to reign as a world’s ‘lesser disaster.’ Just as she was about to speak again, a sharp attack came flying from the side.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
A flashing long sword. A slim skirt and a black zip-up hoodie. Shin Yoosung recognized her immediately.
[Demon Slaying] blazed in Lee Jihye’s furious eyes.
“How dare you do that to my master?”

The majesty of a Historical-grade constellation radiated from Lee Jihye’s entire body. The war god of the sea, stronger than anyone upon its waters. Shin Yoosung realized which stigma Lee Jihye was about to use. Right. Come to think of it, this was a river.
“······Your servant.”
The moment she recited the invocation, jets of water rose all across the Han River, and transparent warships emerged.
“Still has twelve ships remaining······!”
Radiating an imposing fighting spirit, twelve warships appeared above the waves of the Han River. A sight that made one’s knees tremble merely to face it.
The Duke of Loyalty and Warfare’s stigma, Ghost Fleet.
Even beneath the oppressive waves of power from the warships, Shin Yoosung merely smiled, seemingly filled with longing.
“······Right. That was your specialty, unnie.”
“Unnie? You look older than me! What the hell are you talking about?”
“But you still have a long way to go. A captain should be aboard her ship. What are you doing here?”
In an instant, Shin Yoosung was right in front of Lee Jihye, laying a hand against her cheek. She had moved too quickly for Jihye even to resist.
“Poor unnie. Not knowing a thing.”
“What the fuck? How are you so fast······!”
“You wouldn’t know. How Yoo Joonghyuk will use you, how he’ll throw you away. How you’ll die.”
Lee Jihye’s blade flew toward Shin Yoosung. Catching it with effortless ease, Shin Yoosung continued.
“You spent your whole life wanting Yoo Joonghyuk to acknowledge you, and you die on the sea you loved so much. Horribly raped and murdered by the Japanese your sponsor hated so fiercely.”
“All ships, open fire!”
At Lee Jihye’s desperate cry, the twelve warships opened fire simultaneously. Watching the incoming shells, Shin Yoosung smiled.
“Do you know what Yoo Joonghyuk said after he lost you?”
The shells battered Shin Yoosung’s body directly. A thunderous explosion rang out. Appearing where the gunsmoke cleared, she continued.
“Naval battles will be a little more difficult from now on.”

The barrage of countless shells had not inflicted the slightest damage on Shin Yoosung’s white armor (裝甲). [Beast King’s Sensitivity], Shin Yoosung’s unique skill and one of the strongest defensive skills. The white garment enveloping her maintained its proud form, as though it would not permit even the smallest scratch.
“Don’t worry, unnie. That won’t happen in this round.”
Shin Yoosung flashed a white smile.
“Because I’ll send you off without pain.”
Shin Yoosung’s right hand rose silently toward the sky.
“Cry out, King Masswood.”
Then the king of ichthyosaurs, coiled behind her, silently raised its body.
The [Ice Breath] of King Masswood, king of the ichthyosaurs that ravaged the seas.
Rrrrrroooosh!

The bottom of the Han River froze in an instant, and the Ghost Fleet, still firing its cannons, was enveloped in that breath and gradually began to lose functionality. With nowhere left to escape, the ships lost their functionality one after another beneath Masswood’s Ice Breath.
“Let me give you a piece of advice, unnie. Ghost Fleet is powerful, but without water, it’s ultimately meaningless.”
Everything happened in an instant. Shin Yoosung’s fist moving. The sound of something bursting. Lee Jihye dropped her sword, and her limp body shot into the sky.
“Of course, that advice won’t do you any good in this round.”
There was no trace of consciousness left in Lee Jihye’s eyes as she flew through the air, bleeding. King Masswood’s [Ice Breath] was finally spreading across the entire Han River.
“Aaaaagh! What’s happening!”
The incarnations crossing the river screamed at the sudden chill. Swept up in the surging waves of cold, hundreds of people were trapped upon the frozen Han River, doomed to freeze to death.
The one who saved the incarnations as they stiffened helplessly was someone with extraordinary strength who had been watching nearby.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ uses the stigma ‘Great Mountain Smash Lv.5’!]
Lee Hyunsung’s right arm, swollen to an unnatural size, struck the frozen river.
Booooom!
His right arm, swollen almost to bursting, began to break down from his excessive use of Great Mountain Smash. But his efforts were rewarded.
Crrrrraaaack!
The cracked surface of the Han River collapsed, and the influence of [Ice Breath] faltered.
Seizing that opening, the incarnations climbed onto land and advanced on Nodeul Island.
“Waaaaah!”
“Attack!”
Looking at Lee Hyunsung in the center of that army, Shin Yoosung smiled sadly.
“Right, Hyunsung-oppa. I knew you’d be here, too.”
“······Do you know me?”
“Our most reliable shield. You saved my life so many times.”
At Shin Yoosung’s gesture, this time the enormous chimpanzee behind her stepped forward, beating its chest. The grade-5 monster species, Heavy Metal Kong.
Thoooom—!
Its hind foot slammed down in a stomp, sending all the nearby incarnations tumbling. Lee Hyunsung charged at Heavy Metal Kong.
Krrrrraaaah—!

Lee Hyunsung’s swollen arm collided head-on with Heavy Metal Kong’s steel muscles. Crrrunch. Lee Hyunsung’s strength was astonishing. Even with his capillaries bursting and blood flowing from his lips, he did not give an inch against the grade-5 monster.
No, he was actually overpowering it.
Grrrr······?
Watching Lee Hyunsung, Shin Yoosung continued in a numb voice.
“You’re just the same, then and now, Hyunsung-oppa. Yoo Joonghyuk’s most loyal dog······.”
“······Who are you?”
“You saved countless people’s lives, and you protected Yoo Joonghyuk to the very end, until the Iron Blood Dragon’s breath struck you and scattered you into a handful of ashes.”
“Do you know what Yoo Joonghyuk said then?”
As though transplanting her own wounds into others, the tip of Shin Yoosung’s tongue moved like a sharp scalpel.
“A shame to lose such a useful shield.”

Watching the subtle change in Lee Hyunsung’s expression, Shin Yoosung writhed in lonely pleasure. Yes, you should feel it, too. The pain I suffered, the sights I saw. You may not be able to take all of it, but you need to understand this, too.
But she did not know.
That something about this round was different from the round she knew.
Having knocked aside Heavy Metal Kong’s attack, Lee Hyunsung spoke.
“I don’t know what you mean, but I do not follow Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi.”
“What?”
“I am part of Kim Dokja-ssi’s group.”
“Kim······what?”
With a booming crash, Heavy Metal Kong fell.
Her expression hardening, Shin Yoosung approached Lee Hyunsung.
“······What are you talking about?”

With a sound like a drum bursting, Lee Hyunsung’s body flew into the air. Shin Yoosung followed with a ferocious assault on his stomach. A raging storm of ether pierced his tough skin and sent him flying into the middle of the Han River.
It was a blow powerful enough to rupture every one of his internal organs.
Lee Hyunsung would not live to see the rest of the third round.
But a question remained in Shin Yoosung’s mind.
A name she had never heard before, in all her life.
Kim Dokja······.
Who on earth was that?

Tearing open the throats of the incarnations charging at her, Shin Yoosung walked slowly across the frozen river. Frightened incarnations fled, only to be torn to death by monsters’ claws. Despair was gradually settling around their eyes.
Resignation spread among the incarnations as they faced a catastrophe they could not resist.
“Fire!”
Of course, there were those who resisted it.
Having reformed their battle lines, the kings used ranged attack skills to unleash rains of arrows and ether bullets. Shin Yoosung knew them, too.
The King of Beauty, Min Jiwon.
The Maitreya King, Cha Sangkyung.
The Neutral King, Jeon Ildo.

It was strange. They should either have been dead or already become Yoo Joonghyuk’s subordinates. Because all the other ‘kings’ besides Yoo Joonghyuk should have been united beneath the ‘one and only throne’ the moment the fourth scenario ended.
Then what on earth was that?
“Attack! There is only one enemy!”
Whose orders was that ragtag army following?
Where on earth had the [Absolute Throne] gone?
Who ruled this world?
That was when she sensed murderous intent.
With a crackling sound, the ground beneath Shin Yoosung was freezing.
······Ice Breath?
Turning around reflexively, she saw a gigantic ichthyosaur pouring its breath toward her. It wasn’t King Masswood. At her instinctively raised right hand, King Masswood moved.
Grrrrroooo!
Graaaaah!
The two ichthyosaurs seemed to roar at one another simultaneously, then began to collide, their bodies entangled.

Biting and tearing at each other, the king and queen were turning the entire Han River into an enormous octagon. An ichthyosaur large enough to fight King Masswood. As far as Shin Yoosung knew, there was only one.
“······Queen Mirabad?”
She knew the queen was on Earth, but there was no reason for it to attack her.
No, why on earth?
“You’re the future ‘me,’ aren’t you?”
The moment she turned that way, Shin Yoosung’s mind went blank. A time she missed desperately swept through her, shaking her soul.
“Bring ajusshi back to life!”
A girl screaming, and a woman standing in that girl’s way.
“Yoosung, no!”
With a piercing shock, Shin Yoosung the disaster understood the whole situation.
“Haha······Right. I knew it.”
Shin Yoosung lifted herself into the air and approached the girl.
Of course the Yoo Joonghyuk she knew would do this.
That despicable man, who would stop at nothing to achieve his goals, should have acted like this from the beginning.
“Yoo Joonghyuk, you fucking scum······.”
“Yoosung, run!”
Drawing a dagger, Yoo Sangah charged, activating [Hermes Walking Method] and [Arachne’s Web] simultaneously. A strange gleam passed through Shin Yoosung’s eyes.
‘······Olympus?’

But the dagger never reached Shin Yoosung. At a simple gesture, flying creatures swarmed from the gate in the air and descended on Yoo Sangah all at once. Surrounded in an instant, she vanished into the horde of monsters.
Leaving Yoo Sangah behind, Shin Yoosung approached the girl.
The girl’s eyes, filled with fear and anger, were looking up at her. As though bound, she could not move a single step. Shin Yoosung laid a hand against the girl’s cheek.
“So Yoo Joonghyuk really did find the ‘me’ of this worldline.”
“He was going to kill the young ‘me’ to stop the current ‘me.’ Wasn’t he?”
As her deductions fell into place, a terrifying elation seethed in Shin Yoosung’s mind.
The hatred and anger that had briefly faded swiftly returned to their places.
Sure enough, there were things that could not be changed, no matter how many times one returned to the past.
‘Shin Yoosung the disaster’ smiled.
“Hello, past me.”
Just as her hand was about to move.
A powerful blow descended from behind with a deafening roar, engulfing her body. Where the dust cleared, a giant mantis’s scythe gleamed.
“A grade-6 insect king species?”
“Titano! Take her down!”
Gyaaaaah!
The giant mantis’s scythe attacks rained down wildly, churning up the ground as though it were tofu. A fearsome assault. But naturally, it was not an assault that could contend with a ‘disaster.’
“Get lost.”
The ether compressed in Shin Yoosung the disaster’s right arm punched a hole straight through the Titanoptera’s abdomen. Spewing green blood in agony, the giant mantis sank to its knees.
“Titano!”
Furious, Lee Gilyoung leaped from the giant mantis’s head. Yellow slime spread from his body like a parachute, unfurling through the air.
“Go! Antinus!”
Keeeeee!
The parasite that emerged from Lee Gilyoung’s body beat its wings and shot forward.
The grade-5 parasitic species, Parasite.
Shin Yoosung was startled.
“······Antinus?”

Shin Yoosung knew that being, too. Because the place she had destroyed before coming to Earth was the planet Chronos. Antinus was a member of Chronos’s dominant species. A monster possessing the Status of a queen.
She couldn’t believe it.
There was a child who commanded a member of a dominant species as his subordinate?
“You’re quite something, little one.”
Thwap.
But her surprise was brief. Antinus, attempting to infest her, was caught all too easily in Shin Yoosung’s grasp. Antinus’s slime began burning black where it touched Shin Yoosung’s fingertips.
Gyaaaaah······.
It was only natural. Guides could not oppose disasters.
“Talent enough to tame a guide. You’re another child with the talent of a <Lord>. Aren’t you? You’re another one the captain found······.”
Ignoring her question, Lee Gilyoung charged.
“What did you do to Dokja-hyung!”
“What?”
“I asked where my hyung is!”

Charging in, Lee Gilyoung struck her stomach with his fist. It was meant to be his decisive blow, but it was his own wrist that broke. His talent was remarkable, but he was up against the wrong opponent. Shin Yoosung’s white hand seized Lee Gilyoung by the throat and lifted him.
“······Who on earth is this ‘Dokja’?”
Blood was rushing into Lee Gilyoung’s face as he struggled.
“Tell me. Otherwise, you’ll die.”
Then cannon fire sounded in the distance, and the ground beneath her exploded. Shin Yoosung leaped lightly out of the bombardment’s path.
Cannon fire from [Ghost Fleet]? How?
“Gilyoung!”
In the distance, she could see Lee Jihye and Lee Hyunsung running toward her.
A question rose in Shin Yoosung the disaster’s mind.
Strange.
Those blows should definitely have killed them instantly. How were they still alive?
Had she failed to control the force of her blows? She, of all people?
Realizing things had become troublesome, Shin Yoosung tightened her hand around Lee Gilyoung’s throat. Since it had come to this anyway, she might as well ask them instead.
“Goodbye, little one.”

But the moment she clenched her grip, a sharp pain spread through her head, and suddenly her nerves would not obey. Startled, she dropped Lee Gilyoung to the ground. Her trembling right hand was twitching unnaturally.
Had she been infected by the Parasite?
No, that was impossible. A mere grade-5 parasitic species could not interfere with her, a returnee from another worldline. Then······what on earth was this?
Why had her body suddenly stopped obeying her?
At that moment, she heard a voice.
「Stop, Shin Yoosung.」

There was nothing special about the words, yet strangely, the moment Shin Yoosung heard that voice, she felt as though something deep within her heart was crumbling. One side of her heart began to ache unbearably. It was a voice she didn’t know. A voice she certainly didn’t know.
“······W-who the hell are you? Get out of me!”
Why did it fill her with such longing?
Shin Yoosung clutched her head, as though resisting her own sensations.
“Get out! Get out of me!”
Nausea swept over her, and memories she did not know circled through her mind. Worlds that should not be connected, films that could not be connected, were tangling together.
「Yoosung.」
When that voice suddenly brought her to her senses, the young Shin Yoosung stood before Shin Yoosung the disaster.
The young Shin Yoosung’s little lips moved.
“······Ajusshi, are you in there?”
Control the disaster’s body?
I hadn’t planned to do this at first.
My original plan had been something else. But the moment I entered Shin Yoosung, I decided to revise it completely.
[Activating Stage 3 of the exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint.’]
[‘First-Person Supporting Character Viewpoint’ has activated.]
To be precise, I had no choice but to revise it.
「······I can’t accept this.」
「Then what am I? What about all the years I’ve lived?」
「What could ever compensate me for my round?」
Amid Shin Yoosung’s storm of thoughts, I saw the world through Shin Yoosung’s eyes.
I breathed through Shin Yoosung’s nose and killed people with Shin Yoosung’s hands.
I spoke Shin Yoosung’s thoughts in Shin Yoosung’s voice.
I was Shin Yoosung.
[‘Fourth Wall’ shakes violently.]
And I encountered Lee Jihye.
The moment I encountered her, I knew.
That Lee Jihye would die here.
So, for the first time, I tried something I had never done before.
[Interfering with a character’s actions through ‘First-Person Supporting Character Viewpoint.’]
[‘Fourth Wall’ shakes ominously.]

An electric current shot through my head, followed by tremendous pain. Even so, the moment Shin Yoosung delivered the decisive blow, I managed to relax her right hand. The adjustment was so slight that Shin Yoosung did not notice, but I had definitely done it.
Lee Jihye did not die.
[Your understanding of the character ‘Shin Yoosung’ increases.]
The same thing happened again with Lee Hyunsung.
My mind was gradually being torn to shreds, but I began to think that perhaps I could do something with this.
Little by little, I poured in more mental strength, expanding the area of Shin Yoosung’s body I occupied.
And finally, the moment Shin Yoosung’s right hand gripped Lee Gilyoung’s neck.
“W-who are you?”
I succeeded in controlling Shin Yoosung’s right hand according to my own will.
[Your understanding of the character ‘Shin Yoosung’ is very high.]
Someone else’s arm, an arm that was not mine, moving entirely according to my will.
It was an astonishing experience.
“······Ajusshi?”
The young Shin Yoosung asked.
“Get out of me!”

Shin Yoosung’s right arm, which had been under my control, was convulsing. The unnaturally bent arm turned black, and its bulging veins swelled as though they would burst. The young Shin Yoosung rushed toward that blackened arm.
“Ajusshi, it’s you in there, isn’t it? Ajusshi!”

The young Shin Yoosung grabbed the right arm I inhabited. At that moment, powerful sparks erupted around it. Sparks like those that appeared during a probability storm. Startled, people rushed over, but the raging sparks sent them flying.
‘Shin Yoosung the disaster’ and ‘the young Shin Yoosung’ looked at each other at the same time.
Waves of memories were rushing in.
「“Ajusshi.”」
「“Captain.”」
But that shouldn’t have been possible. If ‘Disconnected Film Theory’ was correct, even if the two beings’ existences were connected, their histories could not be.
「“You······can kill me. It’s okay.”」
「“I wanted to survive, too.”」
But, thinking about it, ‘Disconnected Film Theory’ applied only to ‘characters.’
And I had come from outside the novel.
What if my ‘existence’······had served to connect these two girls’ memories?
What if that had connected, however briefly, two films that should never have been connected?
When I closed my eyes, I could feel two Shin Yoosungs holding my hand.
The third round and the forty-first round.
Two different times were facing each other.
「“Could my life be worth living, too?”」
「“But what value could a life like this possibly have?”」
“No! This······this memory······.”
